notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — Two P1 issues: dead MtaStsCache module (confusing duality of cache implementations; will runtime-error if called) and TlsrptRecorder completely unwired from delivery path (RFC 8460 SHOULD unmet). No active correctness bugs in the MTA-STS enforcement path itself. The core enforce/testing/none enforcement logic, DNS lookup, HTTPS fetch, and in-memory cache are correct. The two open children (stoa-2xeks.24 REQUIRETLS inbound, stoa-2xeks.25 E2E test) are legitimately deferred pending STARTTLS inbound (stoa-ovjps.1).
Confidence: 10% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: the session.rs file was too large to read (hit 25k token limit) — REQUIRETLS inbound session handling was not reviewed. Uncertainty driven by: session.rs unseen, relay_queue.rs drain path not read in full. Would raise confidence if: read session.rs lines 1-500 (REQUIRETLS EHLO advertisement) and relay_queue.rs drain loop fully.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — Core enforcement logic is idiomatic. Three findings: missing #[non_exhaustive] on public MtaStsMode, expect() vs unwrap_or_else inconsistency in TlsrptRecorder, one let-else opportunity in policy parser. No unsafe, no gratuitous clones, ownership model is sound (Arc<Vec<String>> for shared MX patterns is correct). Error types are structured with named fields and #[non_exhaustive] on MtaStsError itself.
Rust idiom confidence: 15% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: session.rs body was too large to read in full (only first 150 lines seen); relay_queue.rs drain loop not read past line 200. Uncertainty driven by: unseen code in two large files. Would raise confidence if: read session.rs MAIL FROM handler (lines 420-480) and relay_queue.rs drain loop (lines 200-500).
title: Review: MTA-STS / REQUIRETLS / STARTTLS downgrade protection (stoa-2xeks)
